fields.label: Palliative Performance Scale (PPSv2)
opts: 100%: full ambulation, normal activity and work, no evidence of disease
90%: full ambulation, normal activity and work, some evidence of disease
80%: full ambulation, normal activity with effort, some evidence of disease
70%: reduced ambulation, unable to do normal job or work, significant disease
60%: reduced ambulation, unable to do hobby or housework, occasional assistance
50%: mainly sit or lie, unable to do any work, considerable assistance
40%: mainly in bed, unable to do most activity, mainly assistance
30%: totally bed bound, total care, normal or reduced intake
20%: totally bed bound, total care, minimal to sips
10%: totally bed bound, total care, mouth care only, drowsy or coma
fields.hint: read across the levels for the best fit; ambulation and activity take precedence

sections.title: Goals of care and advance care planning

fields.label: What matters most to the patient
Treatment limits agreed
fields.hint: e.g. no ventilation or ICU, IV antibiotics acceptable

fields.label: Likely last days of life recognised and discussed with the patient and family
Anticipatory medicines available for pain, breathlessness, nausea, agitation and secretions
Hydration and oral intake discussed; sips and mouth care encouraged
Mouth care and pressure care taught to the family
Family know whom to call, day and night
Religious, cultural and personal wishes noted
Family told what to do after death, including the death certificate

sections.title: Red flags
sections.alert: Red flag present. Spinal pain with limb weakness, numbness, difficulty walking or bladder or bowel disturbance: suspected spinal cord compression, contact the oncology or MSCC team immediately for whole-spine MRI within 24 hours. Spinal pain suggesting metastases without neurological features: seek advice within 24 hours and MRI within 1 week. Possible hypercalcaemia: check calcium, albumin and creatinine the same day. Pain crisis: same-day palliative care review. Suspected opioid toxicity: urgent review, and treat as an emergency if breathing is slow.

fields.label: Back or neck pain with limb weakness, numbness, difficulty walking or bladder or bowel disturbance
Severe, progressive or night-time spinal pain in a person with cancer
Thirst, passing a lot of urine, constipation or nausea with new confusion or drowsiness (possible hypercalcaemia)
Severe pain not controlled by breakthrough doses (pain crisis)
Pinpoint pupils, new confusion, myoclonic jerks or slow breathing on an opioid

advice.title: Taking pain medicines
advice.text: Take the regular pain medicine at the times written, even when the pain is less, and use the extra (breakthrough) dose when pain comes through, as explained. Take the laxative every day while on morphine or similar medicines. Keep all medicines safely away from children. Tell us if you need extra doses often, or if you become very sleepy or confused.

advice.title: When to contact the team at once
advice.text: Contact the palliative care team or come to hospital at once for new back or neck pain with weakness or numbness in the legs, difficulty walking, or problems passing urine or stools. Also come for pain that the extra doses do not control, new confusion, severe drowsiness, great thirst or repeated vomiting.

advice.title: The last days of life: advice for family
advice.text: In the last days of life it is usual to sleep more, eat and drink less, and for breathing to become shallow, irregular or noisy. Keep the mouth and lips moist, turn gently, and call the team if there is pain, distress or restlessness. Keep the team's phone number where everyone can find it.
